- `-Pn` = skip host discovery

- `-p 80,443` = scan only those ports

- `-sS` SYN scan
- `-sU` UDP scan
- OS detection `-O`
- Version detection can be unreliable
- traceroute
- host discovery methods like ICMP ping

```bash
proxychains -q nmap -sT -Pn -n -p 22,80 example.com
```

- `nc`

# How to Mutually Exchange Social Housing

A mutual exchange is a great way to move home if you're a social housing tenant. Here's a comprehensive guide to the process:

---

## What Is a Mutual Exchange?

A mutual exchange is a home swap between two social housing tenants. This can occur for a variety of reasons, but often it can be due to needing more space (or sometimes less!), moving for work or to be closer to family.

A mutual exchange is a great alternative for tenants who don't have a high enough priority or banding to be able to access a home through the normal allocation process.

---

## Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

You will need to be a social housing tenant with a secure or assured tenancy to have the right to a mutual exchange. If you have a starter tenancy or a demotion order, you will probably not be eligible to swap – if you think this might apply to you, it's always good to contact your landlord to find out.

Also check the following:
- Your rent account should be clear of all debt and kept up to date throughout the mutual exchange process.
- If you have been served any type of legal notice because you have breached your tenancy in any way, permission for a mutual exchange will not be granted until the situation is resolved. Examples of breaches of tenancy are non-payment of rent, anti-social behaviour, and poor condition of property.

---

## Step 2: Find a Swap Partner

Tenants can swap homes with any other council tenant or housing association tenant that lives anywhere in the UK. It's important to note that you won't be able to swap with a private housing tenant.

There are several ways to find a swap partner:

- **Online platforms:** Sites such as **HomeSwapper** and **Facebook** are widely used.
- **Social media:** To utilise Facebook for the purpose of seeking a swapping party, search for Mutual Exchange in "Groups" and browse the selection of groups set up to assist those seeking an exchange.
- Other ways to find an exchange include word of mouth, local shops, local papers, or social media.

💡 **Tip:** When advertising your home, be sure to include as much detail as possible and recent pictures. This will increase your chances of finding a suitable match.

### MultiSwaps
If you find a match and agree a home swap, you can swap with one tenant or you can try and find a MultiSwap house exchange. A MultiSwap is a swap involving more than two homes, where a swapper moves into the home of a person who is moving into the home of another person, and so on.

---

## Step 3: View the Properties

Your property, including gardens, must be in good condition — you must agree to a property inspection. Visit the property you wish to exchange with, inspecting the condition inside and outside very carefully. Ensure that you check walls, doors, or surfaces that are covered, and that you are completely satisfied with everything, as properties are taken as seen. Also ensure the exchange does not result in overcrowding or under-occupying by more than one bedroom.

---

## Step 4: Apply to Your Landlord

Once you have found another tenant to exchange your home with, you should both contact your landlords, who will provide you with the appropriate forms and information regarding mutual exchanges.

A mutual exchange can only take place with the consent of all landlords. By law, your landlord must make a decision within 42 days of receiving your request to mutually exchange with another tenant.

---

## Step 5: Await Approval

Your Housing Officer will visit you to inspect any alterations you have made and to make sure that the property is in good condition, and will also check your rent account.

An Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) is needed for the mutual exchange to go ahead.

---

## Reasons Your Exchange Could Be Refused

A landlord can only refuse consent for a mutual exchange on specific grounds, for example when the tenant has rent arrears or is in breach of their tenancy, or when the tenancy is subject to a possession order or court proceedings. Other reasons include:

- Your home is too big or too small for your exchange party's needs — exchanges are only accepted where the exchange party will not under-occupy or over-occupy your home.
- The exchange would mean that a home adapted for elderly or disabled people would have nobody living in it who needs the adaptation.

---

## Important Warning

**It is illegal to offer or receive money to carry out a mutual exchange.** If you exchange without asking for permission, you may be forced to move back or have your home repossessed.

---

## If You're Refused

If you are refused a mutual exchange, you can appeal by writing to your landlord. Your appeal will be dealt with according to your landlord's official complaints procedure.

---

**Useful websites:**
- 🏠 [HomeSwapper](https://www.homeswapper.co.uk)
- 🏠 [House Exchange](https://www.houseexchange.org.uk)

Always check with your specific landlord for their exact process and requirements, as these can vary slightly between housing associations and councils.

Dewormer dosage depends on the **type of animal**, the **animal's weight**, the **age**, and the **type of deworming medication** being used. Here is a comprehensive overview:

---

## 📌 General Dosage Formula

The dewormer dosage is calculated based on the **weight of the animal (W)**, the **directed dose per pound (D)**, and the **amount of active ingredient per milliliter (A)**.

Always weigh your pet accurately, as dosing by current weight is critical to avoid under- or overdosing.

---

## 💊 Common Dewormer Types & Dosages

### 1. **Pyrantel Pamoate** (e.g., Nemex-2)
- Pyrantel Pamoate is effective primarily for the treatment of **roundworms** and **hookworms**. It is commonly administered to puppies as young as 2 weeks of age and repeated every 2–3 weeks until 3 months old. The recommended dosage is **5 mg per pound (10 mg/kg)** of body weight, given orally.
- As a liquid suspension, administer **1 teaspoon (5 mL) for each 10 lb of body weight**.

### 2. **Fenbendazole** (e.g., Panacur C, Safe-Guard)
- Fenbendazole is a broad-spectrum dewormer effective against **roundworms, hookworms, whipworms**, and some **tapeworms**. It is typically administered for **3–5 consecutive days** to ensure complete elimination of parasites, and is safe for puppies as young as 6 weeks old, with a recommended dosage of **50 mg per kg of body weight daily**.
- The daily dose for Panacur® C is **50 mg/kg (22.7 mg/lb)** of body weight.

### 3. **Ivermectin**
- Ivermectin is widely used for **heartworm prevention** and is also effective against some roundworms and external parasites. However, it should be used with caution in certain breeds, such as **Collies and other herding dogs**, due to potential toxicity. The usual dosage for heartworm prevention is **2 to 6 mcg per kg of body weight once a month**.

### 4. **Milbemycin Oxime**
- Milbemycin Oxime is a broad-spectrum dewormer effective against **roundworms, hookworms, whipworms, and heartworms**, and is commonly included in monthly parasite prevention products. It is suitable for dogs as young as 4 weeks old, with a dosage of **0.5 mg per kg of body weight** administered once a month.

### 5. **Praziquantel**
- Praziquantel is specifically used for treating **tapeworms** and is often combined with other dewormers (such as fenbendazole and pyrantel) for comprehensive parasite control.

---

## 📅 Deworming Schedule (Dogs & Puppies)

Puppies should typically be dewormed at **2, 4, 6, and 8 weeks** of age and then **monthly until they are 6 months old**.

After the puppy reaches 3 months of age, the deworming frequency transitions to **once every month until the dog is 6 months old**, to ensure continued protection as the immune system develops.

---

## ⚠️ Important Safety Tips

Dewormer tablets require **precise dosing** based on pet weight and parasite type. Over- or under-dosing can cause ineffective treatment or side effects.

Never swap **cat and dog formulations** without label approval — always use species-specific products.

Do not use dewormers in pups younger than 6 weeks, and do not deworm a dog or puppy that is sick.

Check your pet's health status and consult a vet for pregnant or sick animals.

---

Here's a curated reflection on some of the most timeless childhood classics, organized by age group, to help you reconnect with your favorites and share them with your children:

---

## 🍼 Picture Books (Ages 0–5)

### **Goodnight Moon** by Margaret Wise Brown
When *Goodnight Moon* was published in 1947, author Margaret Wise Brown was among the first to center a children's story around everyday objects — from a toy house to a mouse to a bowl full of mush — rather than a fairy tale. Although the book wasn't an immediate hit, it's since sold more than 48 million copies. It is a beloved bedtime companion with soothing, repetitive phrases and gentle illustrations that create a calming atmosphere to help little ones wind down after a busy day.

### **The Very Hungry Caterpillar** by Eric Carle
The unique hole-punched design of Eric Carle's *The Very Hungry Caterpillar* is part of what makes it iconic — but it almost kept it from being published. No U.S. manufacturers were equipped to print the book. Eventually, the publisher found a printer in Japan willing to take on the challenge, and it was first printed in 1969. Today, the book has sold more than 50 million copies worldwide. It's wonderful for introducing toddlers to counting, the days of the week, and the concept of transformation.

### **Where the Wild Things Are** by Maurice Sendak
In print since 1963, Maurice Sendak's *Where the Wild Things Are* has inspired countless imaginations and a live-action movie. The Caldecott Award Winner is often touted as a representation of how children process emotions, but it's the vivid visuals and Max's wild journey that keep this book in heavy rotation.

### **The Snowy Day** by Ezra Jack Keats
*The Snowy Day* broke ground in 1962 as one of the first full-color picture books to feature a Black protagonist, Peter, enjoying the snow in a bright red snowsuit. Author Ezra Jack Keats' bold, collage-style illustrations and the simple delight of an old-school snow day in the city has captivated kids (and adults!) ever since — that's why it's the most-borrowed book of all time at the New York Public Library.

---

## 📖 Early Chapter Books (Ages 5–8)

### **Frog and Toad Are Friends** by Arnold Lobel
Author and illustrator Arnold Lobel published *Frog and Toad Are Friends*, the first book in the Frog and Toad series, in 1970. Toad is a bit of a curmudgeon while Frog is cheerful and relaxed, which adds some comic relief to simple tales about flying kites or telling a story that gives you the shivers.

### **Where the Sidewalk Ends** by Shel Silverstein
Shel Silverstein's 1974 poetry collection for kids, *Where the Sidewalk Ends*, is equal parts profound and downright silly. The poems tackle common childhood experiences, from getting sick to taking out the garbage, but also spin fantastical tales — like a girl who eats a whale! — paired with pen-and-ink drawings.

---

## 🏕️ Middle Grade (Ages 8–12)

### **Charlotte's Web** by E.B. White
Don't miss one of America's top 100 most-loved novels, selected by PBS's *The Great American Read*. This beloved book by E.B. White, author of *Stuart Little* and *The Trumpet of the Swan*, is a classic of children's literature that is "just about perfect."

### **The Secret Garden** by Frances Hodgson Burnett
It remains a popular and beloved story of a child's journey into maturity, and a must-read for every child, parent, teacher, and anyone who would enjoy a fascinating glimpse of childhood. *The Secret Garden* by Frances Hodgson Burnett has remained a firm favorite with children the world over ever since it made its first appearance.

### **Winnie-the-Pooh** by A.A. Milne
This classic tale follows the charming adventures of a lovable, honey-loving bear named Winnie the Pooh and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood. With his companions, including the timid Piglet, the gloomy Eeyore, the energetic Tigger, and the wise Owl, Pooh navigates through various situations and dilemmas, often with humorous and heartwarming results. The book is a celebration of friendship, imagination, and the simple joys of life.

### **Little House on the Prairie** by Laura Ingalls Wilder
The nine books in the timeless Little House series tell the story of Laura's real childhood as an American pioneer and are cherished by readers of all generations. They offer a unique glimpse into life on the American frontier and tell the heartwarming, unforgettable story of a loving family.

---

## 💡 Tips for Sharing These Books With Your Kids

- There is something in these books for children of all ages, and most are enjoyed by adults as well — whether you're trying to find a good book for your child or you're an adult who wants to revisit childhood, a book from this list will be well worth your time.

### 1. Vehicle history and VIN

- Get a **vehicle history report**.
- Check whether it has been in accidents, declared **salvage/flood**, or has odometer issues. The FTC recommends getting a vehicle history report before buying. 

### 2. Open recalls
- Check whether the car has any **open safety recalls** using the VIN. The FTC specifically recommends checking recalls before purchase. 

### 3. Independent mechanic inspection
- Have an **independent mechanic** inspect it before you buy, even if the dealer says it was inspected or “certified.”
- This is one of the best ways to catch hidden mechanical problems. The FTC says a history report is **not** a substitute for an independent inspection. 

### 4. Engine and transmission
Look for:
- rough idle
- smoke from exhaust
- fluid leaks
- warning lights
- delayed or hard shifting
- strange noises

### 5. Fluids
Check:
- engine oil
- transmission fluid
- coolant
- brake fluid
- power steering fluid if applicable  
Dirty, burnt, milky, or very low fluids can signal neglect or damage.

### 6. Tires and suspension
- Uneven tire wear
- Low tread
- Car pulling to one side
- Bouncing, clunking, or poor ride quality  
These can point to alignment, suspension, or accident issues.

### 7. Brakes
- Squealing/grinding
- Vibration when braking
- Soft brake pedal
- ABS warning light

### 8. Body and frame
Look for:
- mismatched paint
- uneven panel gaps
- rust
- signs of flood damage
- welding or bends underneath  
These may indicate prior collision or water damage.

### 9. Interior and electronics
Test:
- AC/heat
- windows
- locks
- lights
- infotainment
- backup camera
- seat adjustments
- dashboard warning lights

### 10. Test drive
Drive it on city streets and at highway speed. Check:
- acceleration
- braking
- steering
- vibrations
- noises
- cruise behavior
- transmission performance

### 11. Title, Buyers Guide, and warranty status
- Make sure the **title** is clean and in the seller’s name.
- If buying from a dealer, read the **Buyers Guide** to see whether it’s sold **“as is”** or with a warranty. Dealers are required to display a Buyers Guide on used cars.

- Compare mileage to service records and vehicle history.

## 🚗 Used Car Buying Checklist

### 1. 📋 Vehicle History & Documentation
- Run the car's Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) through a service like CARFAX or Kelley Blue Book to get a vehicle history report.
- Checking the VIN with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration will tell you whether the car has had a safety recall by the manufacturer. If a recall pops up, ensure the issue has been taken care of before you purchase the car.
- Ask about maintenance records, whether the car has ever been in a crash, and how many owners the car has had.

---

### 2. 🔍 Exterior Inspection
- Check the body for imperfections like gaps, dents, or discolored paint, as these could be signs of reconstruction after an accident.
- Inspect the windows for chips and cracks, the tires for uneven wear, and the tailpipe for black grease.
- Get under the vehicle and check the wheel wells and underbody for rust, which could lead to future problems.
- Make sure the doors are working well and don't show signs of heavy use.

---

### 3. 🛞 Tires & Wheels
- Examine the tire sidewalls for scuffing, cracks, or bulges, and look for dents or cracks on each wheel.
- Check to make sure the spare is in good shape, too, and that the proper jack and lug wrench are present.

---

### 4. 🔧 Under the Hood (Engine)
- Look under the hood for obvious signs of wear, and make sure the engine doesn't appear to have fluid leaks dirtying the block.
- Check the fluids for color and level — black, sludgy oil or cloudy transmission fluid are major red flags that suggest poor maintenance.
- Look for signs of fresh leaks around the engine and transmission. While small leaks can be normal on older vehicles, excessive fluid is a problem.

---

### 5. 🪑 Interior Inspection
- When you first open the car door, sniff the interior. A musty, moldy, or mildewy smell could indicate water leaks — remove the floor mats and check for wet spots on the carpet.
- An acrid smell may indicate that the car was used by a smoker.
- Sit in every seat — upholstery shouldn't be ripped or badly worn, particularly in a car with low mileage. Try all seat adjustments to ensure they work properly.
- Check the upholstery, shifter, and control knobs for unusual wear.

---

### 6. 🚦 Lights & Controls
- Test the turning signals, the headlights, the high-beams, and the brake lights.

---

### 7. 🏎️ Test Drive
- During the test drive, pay attention to how the car handles, any unusual noises, and the comfort of the ride. Make sure to test various driving conditions, including highway speeds and stop-and-go traffic.
- Turn off the radio as you drive to hear any changes or odd noises.
- When braking, listen for grinding or squealing that might point to worn-out brake pads.

---

### 8. 🔢 Mileage
- Consider the miles on the vehicle relative to its age. The average car is driven nearly 15,000 miles per year — if the one you're looking at has a lower average annual mileage than that, it could be considered to have good mileage.

### 9. 🧑‍🔧 Professional Pre-Purchase Inspection
- Before you inspect the car, find a mechanic nearby who can perform a pre-purchase inspection (PPI). Having a professional check for potential issues with expensive parts is always worth the $100 to $150.

# Waking a PC via WiFi — Yes, It's Possible! 🖥️📶

Yes, you **can** wake a PC via WiFi, but it's trickier than wired Wake-on-LAN (WoL). Here's everything you need to know:

---

## 📡 What Is It Called?

If the computer being awakened is communicating via Wi-Fi, a supplementary standard called **Wake on Wireless LAN (WoWLAN)** must be employed.

---

## ⚠️ The Big Caveat

Although just about every WiFi adapter has WOL settings, getting it to work can be difficult, likely because it is not implemented in the system BIOS. Also, Wi-Fi wake-up (WoWLAN) is less reliable and requires specific hardware support.

---

## ✅ Requirements

1. Laptops powered by Intel Centrino processor technology or newer (with explicit BIOS/UEFI support) allow waking up the machine using Wake on Wireless LAN (WoWLAN).
2. Wake on Wireless LAN is supported in **most wireless cards** and can be checked in the Advanced settings of the adapter.
3. For WoL to successfully work, the network interface needs to be able to not just have trickle power in Sleep mode, but also be able to **process the Magic Packet** once it's received over the air.

> ⚠️ **USB WiFi adapters usually won't work** — the "Allow this device to wake the computer" option is typically greyed out for them.

---

## 🛠️ How to Set It Up (Windows)

### Step 1 — Enable WoL in BIOS/UEFI
Wake-on-LAN usually needs to be enabled in the **Power Management section** of a PC motherboard's BIOS/UEFI setup utility.
Access BIOS/UEFI (usually by pressing Del, F2, or F12), navigate to the **Power Management or Advanced** menu, and look for settings labeled **"Wake on LAN," "Resume on LAN,"** or **"Power on by PME."**

### Step 2 — Configure the Wireless Adapter in Windows
Open **Device Manager** (press Windows + type "Device Manager"), expand **Network Adapters**, and double-click the desired **wireless** adapter. Select **"Wake on Magic Packet"** and any other desired options within the Wake on LAN section.

Then:
Select the **Power Management tab** and check **"Allow this device to wake the computer"** and any other desired options.

### Step 3 — Disable Fast Startup
Disable **Fast Startup** in Windows, as this interferes with WOL. Go to **Control Panel → Power Options → Choose what the power buttons do** and turn off Fast Startup.

### Step 4 — Get the PC's MAC Address
Open the **Windows Command Prompt** and enter the `ipconfig /all` command. This displays all network interface information. Find the relevant network adapter and copy its **MAC (Physical) Address** for use in your router's WOL configuration.

### Step 5 — Send the Magic Packet
The router can send a **magic packet** to wake up your computer in sleep/standby mode. You can also use apps on your phone or PC (e.g., WakeMeOnLan, WOL apps) to send the magic packet to the PC's MAC address.

---

## 🌐 Waking Over the Internet (Wake-on-WAN)

If you want to wake your PC from **outside your home network**:
This requires **port forwarding** — configure your router to forward UDP traffic on **port 7 or 9** to the target machine. Since the target PC is powered off, set up a **static ARP entry** in the router so it remembers which IP belongs to the target MAC address even when the device is offline.

---

## 🔁 Alternative: WiFi Bridge Workaround

If WoWLAN doesn't work on your hardware, you can obtain an **Ethernet-to-WiFi bridge adapter**. This uses a second router/WiFi bridge linked to the main router, with the second router connected to the PC. As far as the PC is concerned, it is using Ethernet — making standard Wake-on-LAN fully reliable.

---

### 🔑 Quick Summary Table

| Step | What to Do |
|------|-----------|
| BIOS | Enable Wake-on-LAN / PME |
| Windows | Enable "Wake on Magic Packet" + "Allow device to wake PC" on WiFi adapter |
| Windows | Disable Fast Startup |
| Network | Note the MAC address of your WiFi adapter |
| Sender | Use a WoL app to send the magic packet |
| Internet access | Add port forwarding + static ARP on router |
